correctness.rationale: The exact ordered-copying kernel and positive edge-balance weights on trees yield a bounded fixation martingale. For D_{a,b}, weights are explicit and positive for the full closed mixing interval. The D_{1,3} derivative factors and monotone cubic certify exactly one interior maximum. All trees of order <=5 are bidegreed except D_{1,2}, where four transformed derivative polynomials have uniform strict coefficient signs. D_{1,m} endpoint derivative formulas have opposing signs for all m>=3, and exact rational asymptotics establish an attainable factor-two gain. Standalone SymPy verifies 1514 counted finite-state identities/symbolic checks; the infinite conclusions are proved analytically.

value.rationale: Classifying the monotonicity boundary is explicitly motivated by the primary paper. The five-vertex fork is the first three-degree tree, so it is a natural minimal obstruction to test. The exact sharp six-vertex threshold, complete lower-order exclusion, and an infinite family with asymptotic factor-two gain identify a persistent structural phenomenon not captured by bidegreed monotonicity and not merely a tiny isolated numerical gain.
